fields.meta_title: Membership Form Builder With Tiers and Renewals | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a membership form that checks each applicant's eligibility and tracks every member's renewal date in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Membership Form That Keeps Member Records Current
fields.hero_description: Describe your tiers and who signs off on new members. Emergent builds the membership form and a member database that tracks who belongs and when each membership ends.
fields.features_heading: Six Jobs Behind Every New Member
fields.features_subheading: Joining takes a minute. Keeping each record accurate until the next renewal is the harder part.
fields.feature_1:
Tiers with their own price and questions

Put a household rate and a student rate beside the standard one. Each tier asks only what it needs, such as a school email for students, and the price updates as people choose.
fields.feature_2:
Proof of eligibility read from the upload

Ask for a professional license or a student ID. Emergent reads the name and expiry date off the file, then flags any applicant whose proof has lapsed or does not match.
fields.feature_3:
Approval by a committee or a sponsor

Email each application to the people who decide, or post it in Slack. Every vote is logged on the applicant's row, and the welcome email waits for the approvals your bylaws need.
fields.feature_4:
Member numbers and digital cards

Give each approved member a number in your own format, like LV-0412. Their card page shows the name and end date, and staff at the front desk can confirm who is still active.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders on each member's end date

Track when each membership ends instead of one date for the whole roster. A renewal link goes out by email ahead of each end date, and lapsed members move to a separate list.
fields.feature_6:
An app you can take elsewhere

Publish the form on your own domain or embed it on the site members already visit. Export the full code to GitHub when a developer wants member records inside a larger system.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Groups Admit New Members
fields.tab_content_1:
Proof of license decides the tier

Cedar Valley Society of Surveyors admits Full members at $180 a year and Associates at $90. A Full applicant uploads a state license, and Emergent reads its number and expiry date from the file. A current license is approved at the Full rate. An expired one is offered the Associate tier instead.
fields.tab_content_2:
Seconded twice before a committee vote

Nobody joins Tidewater Rowing Club without two current members vouching for them. The applicant names both seconders on the form, and each one gets an email asking them to confirm. The membership committee sees the application only after both have said yes, then votes at its monthly meeting.
fields.tab_content_3:
Six member cards from one household fee

Bramble Hill Nature Center sells a household membership for $120 that covers two adults and up to four children. One parent fills in the form for everyone. Each of the six people gets a member number and a digital card. Front-desk staff look up any card to see its household and end date.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each renewal gets 30 days of notice

Dues at the Lakeview Neighborhood Association run for a year from the day each household joins. Thirty days before a membership ends, the household gets a renewal link by email. A second reminder follows at seven days. Households still not renewed 60 days after their end date move to the former-members list.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Membership Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the rules for joining first. The fields follow from them.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Price each tier and say who qualifies
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose the proof each tier asks for
fields.howto_step_1_des: Picture one member twelve months after joining. You will want their tier and end date, plus a way to reach them. That record decides the form. Any question whose answer nobody will look at again can stay off it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List every tier with its price and term, such as $90 a year for Associates. Next to each one, write who qualifies. Students need proof of enrollment, households need a list of names and lifetime members need a decision from the board.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Some tiers need evidence before approval, like a professional license or a school ID. Decide which file each tier uploads and what makes it valid, such as an expiry date after today. Tiers that need no proof should skip the upload entirely.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Check your bylaws for who can admit a member. It might be the membership chair alone or a vote of the whole committee. Note whether each person is asked by email or in Slack, and what the applicant hears while they wait.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give Emergent your notes on tiers, proof and approvals in plain English. It builds the form with its approval flow, plus a member table that tracks end dates. Change it later by asking, for example to add a student rate.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run one application through every path. Upload an expired license, leave a sponsor unconfirmed and choose a household with four children. Check that each case lands where the bylaws say it should before any real applicant sees the link.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Set the renewal cycle before launch
fields.howto_step_7_des: Decide when reminders go out and what happens after a membership lapses. A pair at 30 days and seven days before the end date gives members two chances. Publish on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits), then watch the first week of applications on the member table.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits between template galleries (forms.app, Fillout, Jotform, template.net, Pinterest) that hand over a blank set of fields, and membership-software blogs (WildApricot, Raklet) that sell a whole platform. This page treats a membership form as the start of a member record that has to stay true for a year: the tier and its price, proof of eligibility, who approves the applicant, a member number and card, and the date the membership runs out. It answers the PAA questions about cards, types and free memberships from the organizer's side and shows four groups whose admission rules have nothing in common.
tab_stories: A surveyors' society checks each Full-tier applicant's uploaded license, reads its number and expiry date, and approves the applicant at the $180 rate only while the license is current.
A rowing club asks two current members to second each applicant by email and sends the application to its membership committee only once both have confirmed.
A nature center sells a household membership covering two adults and up to four children, and gives every person on it a member number and a digital card for the front desk.
A neighborhood association with dues that run out on different days emails a renewal link 30 days before each one lapses and moves anyone 60 days past their end date to a former-members list.
